provenance.note: A0 modern-regime re-validation. Generated by drivers/mice/{mice_gate,compare_r_reproduce}.py against a PyPI-installed pystatistics==4.6.13, on TWO hosts: CPU+MPS on the Mac (throwaway PyPI venv), CPU+CUDA on Forge (RTX 5070 Ti, cloned env, standing CUDA-testing allowance). mice needed no library code change; 4.6.13 is the shared A0 patch (its mvnmle constant-column fix). Re-establishes correctness under the modern regime (R10/R12/R15), superseding the pre-red-team v3.18.0 report whose correctness was bootstrap-vintage 3.16.3.

reference.name: R mice
reference.what: Multiple imputation by chained equations; the de-facto reference for MICE.

studies.title: CPU vs R fidelity (mixed-type: pmm / logreg / polr)
studies.note: Per incomplete column, pystatistics CPU imputed values vs R mice, compared distributionally (|mean diff|, 1-Wasserstein). Numeric (pmm), binary (logreg), and ordered (polr) columns all match R to within the stochastic-imputation tolerance (W1 <= 0.05).

studies.title: fp32 gate + Rubin coverage + separation + default (CUDA, authoritative)
studies.note: numeric_gate: pooled slopes cover the known truth for cpu/gpu/gpu_fp64; the large single-rep pooled-SE spread is RNG noise (gpu_fp64, same precision as cpu, shows it too). coverage: 40-rep Rubin coverage ~0.92-0.955 across backends (target 0.95), mean-SE within ~2%. separation: a perfectly-separated binary column imputes to ~0.49 class-1, no silent collapse (discrete fits fp64 on CUDA). default: mice(data, seed=0) works.

studies.title: fp32 gate + coverage + separation + default (MPS, secondary)
studies.note: MPS confirmation (second-class to CUDA): coverage 0.945 vs cpu 0.955, separation not collapsed, default works.
